What you missed

On Now
0:55
Polar bear cub in Japan goes viral for his love of traffic cones

A polar bear cub residing in an aquarium in Japan’s Akita Prefecture has gone viral for his love of traffic cones. Mobile phone footage obtained by the Associated Press showed the cub, named Momota, pushing his head inside a cone and poking his mother’s back.

On Now
1:30
World Lion Day: Africa’s big cats face mounting threats from habitat loss and human-wildlife conflict

Africa’s lions are under pressure from shrinking habitat, growing settlements and conflict with people living close to wildlife areas. The warning comes as conservationists mark World Lion Day, with experts in Kenya pointing to retaliatory killings and poisoning as major threats to the continent’s top predator. (AP video by Desmond Tiro)

On Now
1:10
Contiguous US breaks its record for hottest month ever, NOAA says

The contiguous United States sizzled to its hottest month ever last month, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. July averaged 76.89 degrees Fahrenheit (24.94 degrees Celsius) across the Lower 48 states, eclipsing the Dust Bowl’s July 1936 by an eighth of a degree.

On Now
1:07
Farmers in Kenya dispute suspected cyanide poisoning that left 15 elephants dead

Farmers in Kenya’s Kimana area that neighbors Amboseli National Park are disputing claims that 15 elephants died of cyanide poisoning saying the toxin is not present in the pesticides they use. The elephant deaths have intensified concerns over growing human-wildlife conflict in the region due to expanding agricultural activities near the park. Kenya has been widely recognized for rebuilding its elephant population from historic lows to more than 36,000 individuals by reducing poaching and protecting elephants. But conflict between people and elephants remains the second leading cause of deaths after poaching, according to Kenya’s National Elephant Plan.

On Now
1:22
Bulgaria’s flamingo boom boosts birdwatching and conservation

Once a rare visitor, the greater flamingo is booming in Bulgaria’s Burgas wetlands. Its growing population - and the country’s first successful breeding last year - is attracting birdwatchers and shining a spotlight on the need to protect one of Europe’s richest wetland habitats. (AP Video: Valentina Petrova)

On Now
1:34
African Swine Fever threatens Tuscany’s rare Cinta Senese breed

Once rescued from the brink of extinction, Tuscany’s iconic Cinta Senese pig is facing a new existential threat. As African swine fever spreads southward in the region, farmers fear the virus could wipe out one of Italy’s most distinctive native breeds.

On Now
0:48
New images of the sun show its surface in the finest detail yet

Scientists have captured images of the sun’s surface in the finest detail yet. Researchers were able to peek with the help of a telescope on the island of Maui in Hawaii.

On Now
1:16
Scientists certain a SpaceX rocket crashed into the moon

Scientists say they’re certain that a SpaceX rocket has slammed into the moon as predicted. The 5,400-mph crash has yet to be officially confirmed. But space-tracking experts say it’s inevitable that the leftover rocket segment plowed into the moon on Wednesday after drifting off course for the past year.

On Now
2:27
Gene-edited beagles may offer a future option for people with dog allergies

Scientists at a biotech company have used gene editing to switch off a gene that produces the main allergy-causing protein in dogs. It’s the first time this technique has been successful in dogs. Findings were published in the CRISPR Journal. (AP Video/Mary Conlon)

On Now
0:48
Capybaras spotted roaming halls of Brazil state legislature building

Brazil’s beloved capybaras, the world’s largest rodents and social media favorites, made an unexpected appearance inside the legislative assembly building in Brazil’s central-western state of Mato Grosso. Video filmed by a civil servant shows the animals calmly roaming the halls as she tries to gently guide them back outside.

On Now
1:27
Global warming is making summer miserable, but soon El Nino will add to the heat, scientists say

With different parts of the globe aflame in wildfires, deadly heat waves parking over cities, record hot oceans and a strengthening super El Nino, it seems like we’re baking through the hottest year on record. But we’re not quite there — yet. It’s only No. 3 in the record books. But we could be soon.

On Now
1:07
What will happen during this month’s solar eclipse?

For the first time in more than a century, a total solar eclipse would come to mainland Spain. Daytime darkness would descend on Aug. 12 across the Iberian Peninsula, plus slivers of Greenland and Iceland, with a partial eclipse visible in other parts of the Northern Hemisphere.

On Now
1:25
The Mediterranean’s warming waters are drawing hundreds of invasive species

Scientists claimed that climate change, caused mainly by burning oil, coal and gas, is making the Mediterranean Sea hotter, bringing hundreds of new and invasive fish species that decimate indigenous populations. (AP Video by: Maria Grazia Murru; Production by Silvia Stellacci)

On Now
1:38
EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: Scientists’ mission to understand Greenland’s melting glaciers

EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: Scientists’ mission to understand Greenland’s melting glaciers

On Now
1:02
Future of historic listening telescope at risk after funding cut

The UK’s largest telescope is facing an uncertain future after an announcement that funding for a network of telescopes is be withdrawn. The Lovell telescope at Jodrell Bank is part of the e-Merlin array, which UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), a government funded body, says will not be prioritized for further funding after its current agreement ends in March 2028.

On Now
0:58
NASA astronauts and Roscosmos cosmonauts return to Earth, landing in Kazakhstan

A U.S.-Russian space crew landed safely in the steppes of Kazakhstan on Sunday after an eight-month stint on the International Space Station.

On Now
1:20
Caught on camera: a 300 strong humpback whale supergroup gathering to feed

Caught on camera: a 300 strong humpback whale supergroup gathering to feed

On Now
1:15
Endangered newts released into wild at secret location in Spain

Critically endangered newts have been released into the wild in Spain. The 32 Montseny brook newts were reared in a breeding program at the UK’s Chester Zoo.

On Now
1:05
Beloved Japanese macaque Punch celebrates first birthday

Hundreds of birthday cards flew in from all around the world to wish “Punch”, beloved Japanese macaque, a Happy Birthday. (AP video by Mayuko Ono)

On Now
1:16
See how the skeleton of a huge 240 million-year-old amphibian is cleaned

Volunteers worked to clean a 240-million-year-old fossilised amphibian at Warsaw’s Copernicus Science Centre. The bone must be separated from the surrounding rock millimetre by millimetre using a pneumatic chisel. (AP video shot by Rafal Niedzielski)

On Now
1:12
SpaceX launches Starship on another test flight, this time with the most advanced Starlinks

SpaceX’s Starship rocket has blasted off on another test flight, this time carrying 20 of the most advanced Starlinks. Towering more than 400 feet, Starship soared from Texas on Friday, a week after a last-second launch abort. It’s the 13th flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket.

On Now
1:07
Giraffes given a new home in Uganda to escape oil drilling in the country’s largest park

Rangers in Uganda’s largest national park are on a mission to translocate 12 endangered Nubian giraffes. They plan to move the animals 106 kilometers to Ajai Wildlife Reserve. The project is aimed at preserving the species’ population, enhancing biodiversity and diversifying tourism opportunities. About 40% of Uganda’s oil deposits are estimated to be in the Murchison Falls area and within the national park where the giraffes reside. There has been increased activity in the national park including heavy machinery movement despite years of opposition to the oil drilling activities from environmentalists. (AP Video shot by Patrick Onen)

On Now
0:41
Zoo in Germany unveils a young pudu, the world’s smallest species of deer

There was a new addition to the southern pudu herd at Cologne Zoo in western Germany. Named ‘Yenai’, the pudu species is one of world’s smallest species of deer. (AP video and production by Daniel Niemann)

On Now
1:08
A Brazilian bay’s surprise shark nursery sparks conservation project

A Brazilian bay’s surprise shark nursery sparks conservation project

On Now
0:56
US-Russian crew blasts off for stint on space station

A U.S.-Russian crew successfully blasted off on a mission to the International Space Station on Tuesday.

On Now
1:33
Manta tracking project aims to protect Japan’s ocean and coastal rays

Okinawa is one of Japan’s best-known manta ray habitats, but researchers say basic questions remain about how the animals move, where they feed and how they may be affected by warming seas, coral reef degradation and the pressure of tourism. Now a group of divers are deploying a systematic approach to tagging these sea creatures to track their movements and how they live. (AP video shot by Katie Tam)

On Now
0:56
Multiple runners injured on chaotic fifth day of Spain’s San Fermin bull run festival in Pamplona

One runner was gored in the face and many more were fortunate to not be seriously injured during a chaotic bull run at Spain’s San Fermin festival on Saturday.

On Now
0:43
Thai zoo celebrates famous pygmy hippo’s second birthday

A zoo in Thailand celebrated the 2nd birthday of the viral sensation pygmy hippo Moo Deng on Friday, with a large cake made of fruits and vegetables. (AP video shot by Tian Macleod Ji)

On Now
0:54
From deep-sea snails to desert frogs - latest Red List shows no ecosystem is safe from human industry

From deserts to the deep ocean, hundreds of thousands of species are at risk according to the latest IUCN report. The report highlights a growing global biodiversity crisis, with the Red List expanding to 175,909 species, of which 49,505 are now threatened with extinction.

On Now
1:07
A dog’s dinner: Hong Kong allows dogs to eat out at restaurants

It’s a very special dinner time for dogs and their owners in Hong Kong. For the first time in more than 30 years they can go out together to restaurants, thanks to a new policy aimed at promoting the pet economy. (AP video/Alice Fung)
